name: Snowsight Console
thesis: Mirage Console is Snowsight, re-pointed from SQL warehouses at agent data-access. The whole product is ONE three-pane shell that never changes shape: a persistent context bar (workspace · branch · TEST/LIVE), a LEFT OBJECT BROWSER with two trees — RUN HISTORY (top) and DATA CATALOG (bottom) — and a central work area that renders exactly one of two object types: a RUN (opened from history, Profile-forward, with TIME-TRAVEL and LINEAGE as sibling lenses over a single cursor) or a DATA OBJECT (Snowsight-grade schema/grid/profile with a pinned touched-by lineage card). History is the gravity well: you don't "create", you re-open and interrogate. The decisive bet is that the SAME object model and the SAME shell answer the only question that matters — "model mistake or data mistake?" — by letting you cross between a run and the data it touched in one click, in either direction, because both the run's Profile-tree leaf and the data object's lineage card are the identical VfsOp join read two ways (mount_prefix+path over actions[]). Snowsight earned trust by making opaque server-side execution legible AFTER the fact with attributed cost; Mirage does the same on a VERIFIED VfsOp spine, with a hard honesty boundary drawn in pixels: solid = the observed byte (op·path·source·bytes·fingerprint from /replay, the exact diff, the stateAt fold), muted = derived (is_cache=source==ram, op→step pre-stamp, client-computed column profiles, self-reported intent), dimmed = not-yet-emitted (live SQL, latency phases, the provenance graph). The Data View is the showcase — a real catalog tree of 13 mounts where the database mount wears a full Snowflake table skin (schema grid + FK row + virtualized data.jsonl grid with per-column profiling computed client-side) — and the Run View is the query-profile analog where every node is a stamped VfsOp leaf and the primary grain is the INTENT+COMMAND card.
composition: ONE persistent shell, three fixed regions; no page-switcher, no full-route changes — only the center work area swaps its object. (1) TOP CONTEXT BAR (44px, full width, always visible): left = Workspace dropdown (the role+warehouse analog) showing active workspace name + a quiet branch chip [TEST] amber-outline / [LIVE] dimmed-solid; center = breadcrumb of the current object (e.g. "Run · 6f6c5… › Profile" or "Data · /database/users › Schema"); right = global search/Cmd-K pill, a Home glyph, and a small connection dot. Promote (TEST→LIVE) is NOT a button here — it is Cmd-K-only, governance deliberately demoted to the quiet chip. (2) LEFT OBJECT BROWSER (300px, resizable, dark surface-0, the spine of the whole app): a single scrollable column holding TWO collapsible trees with sticky section headers. TOP TREE = "RUN HISTORY" (a flat, filterable, reverse-chron list of Run rows — this is Home-in-the-rail, always present even while a data object is open). BOTTOM TREE = "DATA CATALOG" (the 13 mounts, lazy-expanded via vfsList; database mount flagged with a table glyph). A thin filter/search field pins above each tree. Selecting a Run row opens the Run object in the center; selecting a catalog leaf opens the Data object. The rail is the ONE place both worlds live side by side, so crossing between a run and a path is always a glance away. (3) CENTER WORK AREA (fluid, surface-1): renders a RUN object (lens strip: PROFILE · TIME-TRAVEL · LINEAGE, sharing one ?cursor=idx) or a DATA object (type-aware: TABLE skin or FILE-TREE skin). The center has its own internal sub-shell — a header strip + (for runs) a bottom transport bar + a right inspector that slides in on selection. Everything is keyboard-first: j/k move the active tree, Enter opens, ⌘K jumps anywhere, and a single shared selection (op/path) keeps the run-side and data-side cross-links in sync (backed by the existing consoleStore/sessionRunStore pattern). Visual system reuses the shipped tokens: surface-0..4 dark ladder, mono for paths/bytes/ids, EffectClassTag colors (scratch=muted, durable-internal=captured-green, system-of-record=info-blue, external-effect=simulated-amber), CaptureBadge, mountColor accents.
navigation: All navigation is "open an object from the rail" — there is no app-level routing beyond which object the center shows, mirroring Snowsight where History/Databases are persistent and queries open into the same canvas. RUN-HISTORY → RUN: click a Run row in the top tree (or ⌘K → run id) → center renders the Run, defaulting to the PROFILE lens at cursor=last; breadcrumb becomes "Run · {id} › Profile"; URL ?run={id}&lens=profile&cursor={n} is the permalink. WITHIN A RUN, the three lenses (PROFILE/TIME-TRAVEL/LINEAGE) are a segmented strip that re-skins the SAME center over the SAME cursor — switching lens never loses your selected op (it carries idx). RUN → DATA (the model-vs-data pivot): on any VfsOp leaf (in the Profile tree, the Time-Travel diff, or the inspector) an [open in Data ↗] affordance selects that mount_prefix+path leaf in the DATA CATALOG tree and swaps the center to the Data object; the rail scrolls/expands the catalog to reveal+highlight the path. DATA → RUNS (reverse): inside a Data object's pinned "Touched by" lineage card, each row deep-links back to a Run/Step — clicking re-opens that Run in TIME-TRAVEL with the cursor jumped to that op idx (stateAt fold) and the op ringed. CATALOG → TABLE/FILE: expanding the database mount reveals tables-as-dirs; clicking a table opens the TABLE skin; clicking a slack/s3/github leaf opens the FILE-TREE skin. COMPARE: ⌘K "Compare runs" (or select-2 in the run tree) opens a two-Run split that reuses the lens strip. INVESTIGATION: a saved-findings surface reachable via ⌘K or a rail footer link; "Save to investigation" exists on any op/path/diff. Cmd-K is the universal teleporter: fuzzy across run ids, paths, mounts, and verbs (Open run, Open path, Compare, Promote, Export session, New investigation). Back/forward = browser history of object selections; the rail selection always reflects the center.
homeScreen: HOME = the workspace's RUN HISTORY, and it has TWO faces that are always simultaneously present, never a separate page. FACE 1 — the LEFT-RAIL top tree "RUN HISTORY": a dense, reverse-chron, filterable list (from listSessions/get_runs); each row = [status dot green/amber/red] · run id (mono, truncated) · branch chip [TEST]/[LIVE] · relative time ("12m ago"). A sticky filter bar above it: a search field + quick-filter chips (Branch: TEST|LIVE · Wrote-anything · Touched-mount… · Failed). This tree persists even while a Data object is open, so history is the permanent backbone. FACE 2 — when NO object is selected (cold open / Home glyph), the CENTER renders the FULL run-history table (the Snowsight Query-History grid): columnar, sortable, virtualized, columns = [Status] [Run ID] [Branch TEST/LIVE] [Started] [Steps] [Ops] [Bytes read|written (two mono figures with a tiny read/write split bar)] [Writes] [Mounts touched (effect-class dots)] [Intent preview (first step reasoning, 1-line, muted with a self-reported chip)]. Each row hovers to a faint highlight and opens the Run on click; a right-click/⋯ gives Open · Open in Time-Travel · Compare · Export .mirage-session · Save to investigation. Above the grid: the same filter chips as the rail plus a free-text filter and a count ("38 runs in this workspace · branch TEST"). DATA-CATALOG ENTRY: the center Home also carries a compact "DATA CATALOG" card/strip beneath or beside the grid — a 13-mount summary (each mount: name · ro/rw chip · effect-class dot · derived "touched by N runs" rollup computed from loaded actions[]) — clicking any mount jumps into the Data View. So Home answers "what has this agent been doing to our data lately" at a glance and is one click from both a specific run and the catalog. Empty state (fresh workspace, zero runs): a quiet panel "No runs yet in {workspace}. Runs you execute or import appear here, durable and replayable." with [Import .mirage-session] and [Open Data Catalog].
runView:
RUN VIEW = the Snowflake Query-Profile analog, opened like a query from history, Profile-forward. Center sub-shell, top to bottom: HEADER STRIP — run id (mono) · branch chip · status · started · totals (steps · ops · bytes read/written · writes) · actions [Export .mirage-session] [Compare] [Save finding]; directly under it a LENS SEGMENTED STRIP: �b[PROFILE] · [TIME-TRAVEL] · [LINEAGE], all over one shared ?cursor. The three lenses re-skin the same body:

PROFILE LENS (default) — three columns. LEFT = the OPERATOR TREE: the Workspace›Run›Step›ToolCall›VfsOp waterfall rendered as Snowsight's operator tree, reusing RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock. Each VfsOp leaf node carries solid stats inline: op chip · path (truncated) · source dot · ±bytes · duration_ms · effect-class dot; percent-of-run = op.duration_ms / Σduration (a thin bar, derived → labeled). Arrows/indentation encode Step→ToolCall→VfsOp causality via stamped tool_call_id/run_id. Nodes past the cursor render at ~45% opacity. CENTER-TOP = the "MOST EXPENSIVE OPS" rail (Snowsight's Most Expensive Nodes): a flat descending list of VfsOps ranked by bytes (toggle → duration_ms), row = op · path · mount_prefix · bytes · duration_ms · source; click jumps the cursor to that op idx and rings it in the tree. CENTER-BODY = the selected VfsOp leaf detail + THE INTENT+COMMAND CARD (the directive-1 unit, see intentCommand). RIGHT = the IO-ATTRIBUTION STRIP (Profile Overview analog): bytes-by-source (ram=cache/local vs disk=fetch) bar, cache-ratio (count is_cache / reads, muted "derived"), bytes read vs written, bytes-by-mount colored by effect-class; a DIMMED reserved "latency phases (processing/network/init) — not yet emitted" slot at the bottom, visibly greyed.

TIME-TRAVEL LENS — Redux DevTools over /replay. LEFT = the ACTION LIST (Flat ⇄ By-Step toggle): Flat = virtualized ReplayAction rows [idx · op chip · path · source dot · ±bytes · effect dot · muted cache chip]; By-Step = the same StepCard tree. CENTER = a four-tab inspector over the selected action — ACTION (raw 12-field ReplayAction, solid) · STATE (state.overlay last-write-wins + reads_so_far with "paths only" note + mounts, solid) · DIFF (state.diff via OverlayDiff: write→±bytes/path/mount, read→source/is_cache/fingerprint/revision, solid) · TRACE ("dispatched from" run›step›tool_call›op crumb = the INTENT+COMMAND card). DIFF is default. BOTTOM TRANSPORT BAR (36px, full width): a density mini-map of actions[] (bar height = bytes) with a draggable playhead; ⏮ step-back · ▶/⏸ play (animates over real timestamps) · step-fwd ⏭ · jump-to-end; 1×/2×/4×; right = "cursor #K of M · idx N · 12:04:07.214". SKIP toggle per action re-folds client-side under a "hypothetical: action N skipped — revert" banner (enabled for overlay/reads only).

LINEAGE LENS — NOT its own page; it renders the touched-by JOIN from the run side. CENTER shows the run's distinct touched paths grouped by mount, each with read/write counts; selecting one opens the same touched-by card used in the Data View (every run/step that touched it, cross-workspace-scoped to loaded runs), plus an [open in Data ↗] cross-link. The RIGHT INSPECTOR (shared across lenses) shows, for a selected VfsOp: op·source·bytes·duration (solid), fingerprint·revision (solid, S3-only else "—"), is_cache (muted derived), a [open in Data ↗] bridge, and a reverse "Touched by (this workspace)" mini-list.
dataView:
DATA VIEW = the showcase. Same shell; center renders a catalog-driven, type-aware object. The DATA CATALOG tree (left rail, bottom) lists the 13 real mounts from _console_mounts_detail — each row: prefix (root, slack, sheets, gdocs, tickets, github, pagerduty, datadog, finance, customers, compliance, database, s3) · resource · ro/rw chip · effect-class dot with reversibility tooltip · a subtitle "browsed as file-tree" or "browsed as tables" · a derived "· N runs" touched-by rollup (client union over loaded actions[]); lazy-expand via vfsList (ls). The database mount carries a table glyph and expands to tables-as-dirs (users, invoices, subscriptions, events).

CENTER, TYPE-AWARE, two skins:
TABLE SKIN (database/tables/*) = three columns under a table header. HEADER = table name + a STATS STRIP from stats.json (e.g. users: row_count 500 · 105,590 bytes · last_updated 2026-05-15), and a DISABLED query bar pinned below it (placeholder "SELECT … — live query", tooltip "live query.json / catalog-proxy: schema designed, NotImplementedError"; cursor not-allowed). SUB-TABS: SCHEMA and DATA. SCHEMA = a columns grid from schema.json [name · type · nullable · PK badge], with a FOREIGN-KEYS row beneath ("account_id → subscriptions.account_id", "user_id → users.user_id") rendered as STATIC schema arrows, explicitly labeled "declared schema, not observed dataflow". DATA = a virtualized data.jsonl grid; each column HEADER carries a mini column-profile (type glyph · null% fill/empty micro-bar · distinct count · a 24px sparkline) and is click-to-filter; a muted strip reads "Derived from data.jsonl · column profile computed client-side from N sampled rows · no live SQL". RIGHT COLUMN (≈400px), two stacked panels: (1) COLUMN PROFILE for the selected column — header "computed client-side from N sampled rows"; null-% fill/empty bar; distinct; min/max; TOP-VALUES list for categoricals (plan, status, event_type) or a HISTOGRAM for numeric/timestamptz (created_at, last_login, amount, mrr, timestamp), bars click-to-filter the grid. (2) LINEAGE "TOUCHED BY" card (see intentCommand/lineage) pinned at the bottom; below it a ReservedMetadataStrip [fingerprint · revision · consistency] showing "—" on this disk-backed table (with "S3-only via ETag" hint), never zero-filled.
FILE-TREE SKIN (slack, s3, github, datadog, sheets, gdocs, tickets, customers, finance, compliance) = a breadcrumb path bar + a vfsFile preview pane (text-decoded content, monospace, with an honesty strip "preview only · text decode · no binary/truncation guarantees") + the SAME right column: a lightweight metadata panel (size from vfsFile, mode, effect-class, fingerprint/revision "—" unless S3-like) and the LINEAGE "Touched by" card. Selecting a file selects its mount_prefix+path so the touched-by join and the run-side cross-links stay in sync.
intentCommand:
THE INTENT+COMMAND CARD is the run-inspection grain (directive 1), used in the Profile center-body, the Time-Travel TRACE tab, and (compactly) in the By-Step list. Grain = Step(intent) → [ToolCall(command) → VfsOp(effect)] — a collapsible card, NOT a rigid 1:1, because one step can emit several commands. Layout:
┌ Step N · ●step-name · 1.2s · 2 cmds ─────────────────────────┐
│ INTENT  [muted chip: self-reported · AG-UI THINKING]         │ ← steps.reasoning, 2-line clamp; ▸ verbatim expands full reasoning (getSessionTrace). If empty: "No stated intent for this step" (muted italic) — never fabricated.
│   "read the live checkout dashboard to correlate the deploy"  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▾ COMMAND  $ cat /s3/dashboards/checkout.json   exit 0 · 6ms  │ ← tool_calls.args+exit_code (SOLID); ▸ full stdout expands tool_calls.result
│     └ EFFECT  read · /s3/dashboards/checkout_2023.json        │ ← the VfsOp leaf (SOLID); click → cursor jumps to that action's Diff
│              s3 · 4.2 KB · rev v3 · fp 9a1f · [cache]          │ ← fingerprint/rev SOLID only when present (S3-like); cache chip MUTED (derived source==ram)
│   [⚑ INTENT≠EFFECT  'live' intent vs cached read of a 2023 path] ← SOLID amber flag, conservative heuristic
│ ▸ COMMAND  $ jq '.errors' …                     exit 0 · 2ms  │ ← second command, independently collapsible
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: three tiers — (default) intent line + command + one-line effect; (▸) verbatim reasoning / full stdout; (effect row click) jump the time-travel cursor to that exact VfsOp. INTENT≠EFFECT FLAG: computed conservatively — fires only when intent text says "live/latest/current" but effect is is_cache=true, or names path A but the op read path B; rendered as a solid amber chip "possible mismatch"; NEVER fires when intent is absent (no claim = no contradiction). This flag IS the model-vs-data fast-path: mismatch → suspect model error; intent matches but data wrong → data error, pivot via [open in Data ↗] to inspect fingerprint/revision.
INTENT≠EFFECT vs HONESTY: the intent row carries a muted "self-reported" chip and reserves the exact slot to flip to a solid "observed intent" chip when a cognition plane lands — zero layout change. Effect and command are always solid (observed I/O). The LINEAGE "Touched by" card (reused in Data View + run inspector) renders the client-side join: header "Touched by N runs · M ops [●read R][●write W][src facets]", rows grouped by run_id → tool_call_id with each leaf {op·source·bytes·is_cache(muted)·fingerprint(if present)}, a hop-2 "Co-touched in these runs: /other/path …" line (labeled co-occurrence, not downstream), and a footer "op-level lineage from observed VfsOps in this workspace's runs · not a transitive provenance graph"; a [graph ⤢] opens a visibly DIMMED mini-graph labeled "preview · op-level, not provenance".

signatureInteractions: The model-vs-data pivot in one click: from any VfsOp leaf [open in Data ↗] swaps the center to that path's Data object and lights its Touched-by card; from a Touched-by row, jump straight back into that Run's Time-Travel at the exact op idx (stateAt fold) with the op ringed. Same join, both directions, one shared selection.

Most-Expensive-Ops → cursor: click the top-ranked VfsOp in the Profile rail and the operator tree rings it + the Time-Travel cursor lands on its idx — triage 40 ops by reading the top three rows (Snowsight's Most Expensive Nodes, on a real byte spine).

Lens switching over ONE cursor: toggling PROFILE↔TIME-TRAVEL↔LINEAGE re-skins the same center at the same idx — you never lose the op you're staring at, and the permalink (?run&lens&cursor) reconstructs it exactly.

Time-travel scrub: drag the bottom mini-map playhead and watch state.overlay grow (last-write-wins) and reads_so_far accumulate; toggle SKIP on an action for a pure client-side re-fold what-if under a 'hypothetical' banner — never a re-drive.

Client-side column profiling on a real grid: select a column in the data.jsonl grid and the right panel computes null%/distinct/min-max/histogram from sampled rows, click a histogram bar to filter the grid — labeled 'computed client-side, no live SQL' so it's never mistaken for engine stats.

INTENT≠EFFECT flag as the fast triage: a solid amber chip fires only when self-reported intent contradicts the observed op (says 'live' but is_cache=true, or names a different path), pointing you at model-error vs data-error before you read anything else.

Cmd-K as universal teleporter: fuzzy across run ids, paths, mounts, and verbs (Open run, Open path, Compare, Promote TEST→LIVE, Export .mirage-session, New investigation) — the only place promote lives, keeping governance demoted.

Export/Import .mirage-session: serialize actions[] + getSessionTrace + mount manifest to a file a teammate re-imports to scrub offline, deterministically — labeled 'scrub limited to overlay/reads/run; backing pinned at stand-up'.
risks: Two-tree left rail + central object swap risks feeling like two apps bolted together; the cross-links (open-in-Data / touched-by deep-links) and shared selection MUST be tight and instant or the 'one shell' illusion breaks and it reads as tab-switching.
Run history grid can firehose — with many runs the columnar list needs strong default filters (this branch, wrote-anything, failed) and virtualization, or Home becomes noise instead of a worklist.

The DISABLED query bar in the Table skin is a constant temptation to imply SQL; if the tooltip/affordance is weak, users will try to type and feel the worksheet metaphor lying. Must be unmistakably inert (greyed, not-allowed cursor, explicit NotImplementedError note).

Client-side column profiles and the touched-by join are computed over LOADED runs/sampled rows only; 'Touched by N runs' and distribution stats can silently mislead if the 'this workspace's loaded runs / sampled rows' scoping label is ever dropped — honesty rides entirely on those muted captions.

is_cache / op→step pre-stamp / latency-phase are derived-or-absent; if the muted vs dimmed visual tiers blur together, the whole credibility bet (solid=observed) collapses — the three honesty tiers need genuinely distinct, legible styling, not just opacity.

Lineage-as-a-lens (not a nav item) plus a dimmed [graph ⤢] preview risks users expecting a real provenance graph; the 'op-level, not provenance' labels and the deliberately-greyed graph must be loud, or it over-promises Databricks-grade lineage that doesn't exist.

The INTENT≠EFFECT heuristic can false-positive/negative on the demo (no semantic ground truth); over-firing erodes trust. It must stay conservative, labeled 'possible mismatch', and silent when intent is absent.

Profile %-of-run from duration_ms is derived and cache reads emit no op — the operator tree's cost attribution can look authoritative; the 'derived' label on the percent bar and the absence of phantom cache-hit nodes are load-bearing and easy to forget.

name: Mirage Console — "The Workbench" (Paradigm B: IDE Workbench)
thesis: The workspace is a project you live inside, not a series of pages you visit. The entire console is ONE docked shell of cross-filtering panes over a single shared selection — `{ workspaceId, branch, runId, opIdx, path }` (one store, the existing consoleStore/sessionRunStore pattern). Pick an INTENT+COMMAND card in the Run pane and its `cursor_op` instantly cross-highlights: the Data pane scrolls to and rings the `mount_prefix+path` it touched, the State pane re-folds to `stateAt(idx)`, the Inspector swaps to that VfsOp leaf, the transport playhead snaps to `idx`. Click that same path in the Data pane and the reverse touched-by lights up every run that touched it. The three lenses (PROFILE / TIME-TRAVEL / LINEAGE) are not pages and not even tabs — they are DOCKABLE PANES the engineer arranges, exactly like VS Code's Source Control / Run-Debug / Search live as panels not routes. Run-history is Home; the data catalog is a permanent left rail one keystroke away; Cmd-K is the spine. Everything obeys the honesty tiers structurally: solid borders for ground-truth VfsOp leaves/diffs/the mount_prefix+path join/the stateAt fold; muted (dashed, 70% text) for derived (is_cache, self-reported intent, client-computed column profiles, pre-stamp op→step); dimmed (40%, "not yet" ghost) for unemitted (hosted cognition, provenance graph, live SQL, latency phases). The reward is an engineer who never loses their place: review beats re-running because the whole project — every run, every byte, every diff — is laid out in front of you, cross-linked, permalinkable (`?run=&op=&path=&docks=`), and exportable as one `.mirage-session.json`.
composition:
ONE persistent docked shell — never a page swap. Four zones in a CSS grid that the user resizes by dragging dividers (layout persisted per-workspace in localStorage, like VS Code):

(1) TOP — Workspace Context Bar (sticky, 44px, full width): `Workspace ▾` dropdown (the Snowflake role+warehouse analog) · branch chip `TEST`/`LIVE` (quiet, amber outline only for LIVE) · breadcrumb `run_a1f8 › step 3 › op #12` reflecting the shared selection · global `⌘K` button · right side: dock-layout presets (`Triage` / `Debug` / `Catalog`) + Export-session button. This bar scopes EVERY pane identically and never moves.

(2) LEFT — Activity Rail (48px icon strip, VS Code-style) + collapsible Explorer (260px). Icons toggle what the Explorer shows: ⌂ Run History (Home), ⛁ Data Catalog, ⎇ Runs-in-this-session, ★ Investigation, ⊞ Compare. Only ONE Explorer panel shows at a time; the icon strip is always visible so you cross from runs→data without losing the shell. The Explorer is a tree/list, never the main content.

(3) CENTER + RIGHT — the DOCK GRID: a tab-and-split workbench (like a VS Code editor group). Panes are draggable tabs that can be split horizontally/vertically. The pane TYPES are: `Run` (intent+command stream), `Data` (catalog table/file detail), `Profile` (operator-tree lens), `Time-Travel` (action list + state lens), `Lineage` (touched-by lens), `Inspector` (the selected-atom detail), `Compare`. The user docks any combination. Default `Debug` preset = Run pane (center-left) | Inspector (center-right) | Time-Travel state pane (bottom strip). The lenses are entered by adding a pane (`⌘\` to split, then pick lens) or by clicking a lens chip in the Run pane's header which swaps the active pane's body — NOT by routing away.

(4) BOTTOM — global Transport Bar (36px, full width, present whenever a run is selected): density mini-map of `actions[]` (bar height = bytes) with a draggable playhead bound to the shared `cursor`. ⏮ ▶/⏸ ⏭, 1×/2×/4×, and `cursor #K of M · idx N · 12:04:07.214` from `cursor_op.timestamp`. This is the single time axis every pane reads from.

THE CROSS-FILTER CONTRACT (the soul of Paradigm B): every pane subscribes to one selection store. Setting `opIdx` (from anywhere) triggers `getReplay(session, idx, run)` → its `state.cursor_op`/`diff` flow to Inspector, State pane re-folds, Data pane resolves `cursor_op.path` and rings it, Lineage recomputes touched-by, Profile rings the node, transport snaps. Setting `path` (from Data/Lineage) filters the loaded `actions[]` by `mount_prefix+path` and lights the reverse list. Hovering cross-highlights (faint); clicking commits (rings + breadcrumb). No pane is ever stale.
navigation:
There is almost no "navigation" in the page-router sense — that's the paradigm's whole point. Movement is (a) changing the shared selection, which ripples through docked panes, and (b) docking/undocking panes.

• Home → a Run: in Run-History Explorer (or the center Home pane), click a run row → the dock grid hydrates with the `Debug` preset for that run (`getReplay` + `getSessionTrace`), context-bar breadcrumb updates, transport appears. You did not leave Home — the Explorer rail still shows run history; you can click another run and the panes re-bind. (Permalink: `?run=run_a1f8&docks=run|inspector`.)

• A Run → its Data: from any VfsOp leaf row or the Inspector, click `↗ Data` on the `mount_prefix+path`. This OPENS A DATA PANE docked beside the Run pane (split), Data pane resolves the path in the catalog tree, renders the table/file detail, and its Lineage card lights the reverse touched-by including the current op (ringed). Run pane stays put — you now see both, cross-linked.

• Data → Runs (reverse): in the Data pane's Lineage "Touched by" card, click a run/step row → shared `runId`+`opIdx` set → if a Run pane is docked it scrolls+rings that op; if not, one docks. Bidirectional, both panes stay visible (the Databricks "lineage-tab-on-table AND upstream-link-on-job" move).

• Switching lenses on a run: click `Profile · Time-Travel · Lineage` chips in the Run pane header → the pane body swaps lens in place (same run, same cursor). Or `⌘\` splits and you pick a different lens so two lenses sit side-by-side over the SAME cursor (e.g. Profile + Time-Travel — scrub in one, watch cost rank in the other).

• Compare: ⊞ from the rail or `⌘⇧C` on a run → a Compare pane docks; pick run B; it renders the two action streams aligned. Selecting an op in either side cross-highlights the matching path in the other.

• Investigation: ★ rail opens the saved-findings Explorer; `⌘⇧S` from any pane snapshots the current `{run,op,path,docks,cursor}` permalink + note into the notebook.

• Cmd-K is the universal jump: fuzzy over runs, paths, mounts, ops, saved findings, lens/dock commands ("split Profile right", "dock Data"), and governance ("Promote to LIVE" — Cmd-K-only, demoted). Selecting a result sets the shared selection or runs the dock command.
homeScreen:
HOME = Run-History Workbench. On first load (no run selected), the dock grid shows a single full-width `Run History` pane; the left Activity Rail defaults to ⌂ with the run-history Explorer mirrored as a compact list. This is the Snowsight query-history-as-first-class-objects surface, sourced from `listSessions` + per-run rollups from `get_runs`/`get_steps`/`get_tool_calls`/`get_vfs_ops`.

LAYOUT — three bands in the Run History pane:
• Top: a filter/worklist bar — facet chips `branch: TEST|LIVE` · `wrote anything` (write-count>0) · `touched mount ▾` (the 13 mounts) · `failed` (any exit≠0) · `intent≠effect flagged` (muted chip, heuristic) · free-text. A right-aligned `view: list ⇄ matrix` toggle (Databricks Runs matrix vs list).

• Center: the run table — columns = `[status dot] · run id (mono, click=open) · branch chip · started (relative) · steps · ops · total bytes · writes · top mounts (effect-class dots) · ⚑`. Each row is dense (single line), hover reveals a 1-line intent preview ("read live checkout dashboard…" — first step's `steps.reasoning`, muted). The `⚑` column shows an amber flag when the heuristic intent≠effect fired in that run. Rows are durable/permalinkable (each is `?run=…`). Matrix view swaps the center for a status grid (rows=runs, cells=step-status) for scanning many runs at once.

• Left Explorer (the ⛁ catalog is one icon-click away, never more): when ⌂ is active it shows runs grouped by day; one click on ⛁ swaps to the Data Catalog tree (13 mounts) so "the data catalog is one keystroke away" is literal. A `Recents` group at the top (server-side, survives switches — stronger than Databricks' browser-only Recents; say so in a tooltip).

EMPTY/HONEST STATES: if `listSessions` is empty → EmptyState "No runs in this workspace yet — start one or import a .mirage-session.json". Counts that are derived (e.g. flag column) carry the muted styling. Bytes/ops/writes are solid (straight from the store). Clicking any run hydrates the dock grid into the Debug preset without leaving the shell.
runView:
RUN VIEW is not a page — it's the dock grid bound to a `runId`, defaulting to the `Debug` preset: [Run pane | Inspector] over [State strip], with the Transport bar at the bottom. Every region shares the cursor.

RUN PANE (center-left) — the INTENT+COMMAND stream (built on RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock). Header: `run_a1f8 · TEST · 7 steps · 23 ops · 1.2 MB` and a lens chip group `[Stream] Profile Time-Travel Lineage` (Stream = the default intent+command list; the others swap THIS pane's body to a lens over the same cursor, or `⌘\` to keep Stream and open a lens in a split). Body: vertical stream of INTENT+COMMAND cards grouped `Step(intent) → [ToolCall(command) → VfsOp leaves]`. Cards past the cursor render at ~45% opacity with a "not-yet-executed" left border (the time-travel tie-in). Selecting any VfsOp leaf row sets `opIdx` → ripples everywhere. Selecting a card's step header sets the step (multi-op) selection.

INSPECTOR PANE (center-right) — the selected-atom detail, four altitude tabs over `cursor_op` exactly mirroring Redux DevTools (Action/State/Diff/Trace): 
 · DIFF (default): the `state.diff` rendered via OverlayDiff — write→`{path, +added_bytes, mount_prefix, effect-class dot, CaptureBadge}`; read→`{path, source dot, is_cache (muted), fingerprint·revision OR "— S3-only" on disk mounts}`. Top of this tab pins the compact INTENT+COMMAND card for the op's owning step. 
 · STATE: the fold at idx — Overlay node (`state.overlay`, last-write-wins, OverlayDiff renderer) + Reads-so-far node (`state.reads_so_far` with muted "paths only — no per-read bytes") + Mounts node + a dimmed "backing snapshot (not yet)" stub. 
 · ACTION: raw `ReplayAction` JSON (all 12 fields, solid). 
 · TRACE ("dispatched from"): the causality crumb `run_a1f8 › step-… › tool_call tc-… › this op` (each segment clickable) + a `↗ Data` jump to the path's Data pane + a mini reverse touched-by — this tab is where the VfsOp→data bridge and the full intent+command live.

STATE STRIP (bottom dock) — a thin Time-Travel-lite: the overlay summary at the current cursor (N paths written, M read) so you always see "what's true now" while scrubbing, even before you open the full Time-Travel lens.

The three FULL lenses (when docked/swapped) are detailed in screens: Profile = operator tree + Most-Expensive-Ops rail + IO strip; Time-Travel = full action list + transport-driven scrub + skip what-if; Lineage = touched-by both directions. All three read the same `runId`/`cursor`, so docking two of them side-by-side (e.g. ⌘\ → Profile right of Time-Travel) lets you scrub on the left and watch the cost ranking re-highlight on the right — the Paradigm-B payoff.
dataView:
DATA VIEW is a Data PANE (dockable, openable from the ⛁ rail or any `↗ Data` jump), Snowsight-grade, three internal regions inside the pane (the pane itself can be split beside a Run pane):

LEFT (catalog tree, ~280px) — the 13 real mounts from `_console_mounts_detail` via lazy `vfsList`. Each mount row: `prefix` · `resource` · `ro/rw` chip · effect-class dot (reversibility tooltip from effectClass lib) · subtitle "browsed as file-tree | table" · derived "touched by N runs" rollup (muted; client union over loaded runs' `actions[]`). The `database` mount expands to `tables/{users,invoices,subscriptions,events}` flagged with a table glyph (Snowflake skin); slack/s3/github expand as file trees.

CENTER (type-aware detail):
 TABLE skin (database tables) — header = table name + Stats strip from `stats.json` (`users: row_count 500 · 105,590 B · last_updated 2026-05-15`, solid). A DISABLED query bar directly below (tooltip: "live query via query.json / catalog-proxy — schema designed, NotImplementedError"; cursor not-allowed). Sub-tabs: `Schema` (columns grid from `schema.json`: name·type·nullable·PK; plus a foreign_keys row rendered as a static caption `account_id → subscriptions.account_id` — labeled "static schema FK, not observed dataflow") and `Data` (virtualized `data.jsonl` grid; each column header carries its mini column-profile + click-to-filter). Muted footer: "derived from files · column profile computed client-side · no live SQL."
 FILE-TREE skin (slack/s3/github) — breadcrumb + `vfsFile` (cat) preview in a monospace viewer + honesty strip: "preview only · text decode · no binary / truncation handling."

RIGHT (~360px, two stacked cards):
 COLUMN PROFILE (for the selected column) — header "computed client-side from N sampled rows" (muted). Body: null-% fill/empty bar, distinct count, min/max; then a click-to-filter histogram for numeric/timestamptz (`created_at`, `last_login`) or top-values list for categoricals (`plan`, `status`). All COMPUTED from `data.jsonl` (stats.json is table-level only) and labeled so.
 LINEAGE — "Touched by N runs · R read / W write": the `get_vfs_ops`-by-`mount_prefix+path` client join. Rows grouped by `run_id` then `tool_call_id`: `op · idx · bytes · source · duration_ms` + run/step deep-link, fingerprint/revision SOLID only when present (omitted on disk mounts, never zero-filled), `is_cache` muted, op→step tagged "inferred" only where pre-stamp. A hop-2 line "Co-touched in these runs: /s3/metrics/latency.json · …" labeled co-occurrence (not downstream). Footer: "op-level, this workspace's loaded runs · not a transitive provenance graph." A `[graph ⤢]` button opens a DIMMED mini-graph preview (center=path, left=read runs, right=write runs) labeled "preview · op-level, not provenance." Clicking any lineage row sets shared `runId`+`opIdx` → if a Run pane is docked it rings that op (stateAt idx); else one docks. Below: a ReservedMetadataStrip (fingerprint/revision/consistency = dash on disk, S3-only via ETag).

CROSS-FILTER: when the shared `opIdx` points at a path this pane is showing, the catalog row + (if table) the touched cell region rings; when you select a column or row here, nothing leaves the pane (data inspection is local) but selecting a lineage row drives the global selection.
intentCommand:
THE INTENT+COMMAND CARD — the run-inspection grain, used in the Run pane stream AND the Inspector's Trace tab. Grain = `Step(intent) → [ToolCall(command) → VfsOp leaves]`, a collapsible card (never a rigid 1:1, because one agent iteration emits THINKING then several exec lines).

LAYOUT (collapsed default):
┌─ Step 3 · [● status] "correlate the deploy" · 1.2s · 2 cmds ─────────────┐
│ INTENT  ⟨muted chip: self-reported · AG-UI THINKING⟩                      │  ← steps.reasoning, 2-line clamp
│   "read the live checkout dashboard to correlate the deploy"             │
│   (if empty → muted italic "No stated intent for this step")             │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▾ COMMAND  $ cat /s3/dashboards/checkout.json            exit 0 · 6ms     │  ← tool_calls.args + exit_code (solid)
│     └ EFFECT  read · /s3/dashboards/checkout_2023.json                    │  ← the VfsOp leaf (solid); click → opIdx
│              s3 · 4.2 KB · rev v3 · etag-9a1f · ⟨cache⟩                    │     fingerprint/rev solid (S3); cache muted
│     ⚑ INTENT≠EFFECT — stated "live" vs cached read of a 2023 path         │  ← solid amber flag, conservative heuristic
│ ▸ COMMAND  $ jq '.errors' …                              exit 0 · 2ms     │  ← 2nd command, collapsed (proves grain)
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: INTENT has `▸ verbatim` → expands full `steps.reasoning` (from `getSessionTrace` THINKING fold). Each COMMAND has `▸ full stdout` → expands `tool_calls.result`. EFFECT row click → sets shared `opIdx` (rings everywhere). The whole card is the Trace-tab content too, so "why did this op fire" is one tab away from any selected leaf.

INTENT≠EFFECT FLAG (honest heuristic, never a verdict): fires ONLY when intent text exists AND contradicts the observed op — e.g. reasoning contains live/latest/current but `is_cache==true`, or names path A but the VfsOp read path B. Tone: solid amber (this comparison IS observed: stated-string vs ground-truth leaf). Tooltip: "possible mismatch — heuristic over self-reported intent vs observed op, not a semantic verdict." Never fires when intent is absent (no claim to contradict).

PROVENANCE TIERS ON THE CARD (the intent≠effect honesty): INTENT row = MUTED (dashed underline + "self-reported · AG-UI THINKING" chip) because the system prompt only says the agent "may show your reasoning"; it degrades to "No stated intent" when empty and UPGRADES IN PLACE to a solid "observed intent" chip with zero layout change when a cognition plane lands (reserved slot). COMMAND and EFFECT rows = SOLID (observed I/O: `tool_calls.args`/`exit_code` and the VfsOp leaf). The flag sits between them, comparing the muted claim to the solid effect — which is exactly why it can only ever be "possible," and the card says so.

signatureInteractions: CROSS-FILTER SELECT (the paradigm's signature): click an INTENT+COMMAND EFFECT row in the Run pane → shared `opIdx` set → `getReplay(session, idx, run)` re-folds → Inspector swaps to that VfsOp (Diff/State/Action/Trace), Data pane rings `cursor_op.path`, Lineage recomputes touched-by, Profile rings the node, Transport playhead snaps. One click, every docked pane re-binds, breadcrumb updates. Hover = faint cross-highlight; click = committed ring.

DOCK A LENS (lenses are panes, not pages): `⌘\` splits the active pane and you pick Profile/Time-Travel/Lineage, OR click a lens chip to swap the current pane body in place — both keep the same `runId`+`cursor`, so you can sit two lenses side-by-side over one cursor (scrub Time-Travel left, watch Most-Expensive-Ops re-rank right).

BIDIRECTIONAL DATA⇄RUN BRIDGE: from a VfsOp leaf, `↗ Data` docks a Data pane on that exact `mount_prefix+path`; from the Data pane's touched-by card, click a run row to drive the global selection back into a Run pane. Both panes stay visible and stay in sync (the Databricks lineage-on-table + upstream-on-job move, made live).

SCRUB THE FOLD: drag the bottom Transport playhead over `actions[]` (bar height=bytes) → cursor moves → State strip + State tab re-fold via `stateAt(idx)`, Run-pane cards past the cursor dim to 45%, Data/Profile/Lineage re-highlight live. Play at 1×/2×/4× animates over real `cursor_op.timestamp` spacing.

SKIP-ACTION WHAT-IF: in the Time-Travel pane, toggle skip on an action → client-side re-fold of `actions[]` minus that idx under a solid banner 'hypothetical: action N skipped — revert'. Enabled only for overlay/reads (recomputable); disabled with tooltip for backing-FS-dependent state (deferred). Labeled a state-reconstruction what-if, never a re-drive.

INTENT≠EFFECT TRIAGE: the amber ⚑ on a card (and the Home run-table column) jumps you to the mismatch; the flag compares the muted self-reported intent string to the solid VfsOp leaf and says 'possible mismatch — heuristic', the core 'model mistake vs data mistake?' fast-path.

SNAPSHOT TO INVESTIGATION: `⌘⇧S` from any state captures the full permalink `?run=&op=&path=&cursor=&docks=` + a note into the saved-findings notebook — turning a live cross-filtered workbench layout into a shareable durable artifact.

EXPORT/IMPORT SESSION: Export button serializes `actions[]` + `getSessionTrace` events + mount manifest to `.mirage-session.json` (generalizing TrajectoryPage.exportJson); Import re-hydrates a teammate's workbench to scrub offline, labeled 'scrub limited to overlay/reads/run; backing pinned at stand-up'.

LAYOUT PRESETS + PERSISTENCE: Triage/Debug/Catalog dock presets in the context bar instantly rearrange panes; custom layouts persist per-workspace (localStorage) so the engineer's workbench is exactly where they left it across switches (server-side workspace→session persistence backs the run data).
risks: DOCK COMPLEXITY vs the keyboard-first promise: a freely splittable VS Code-style workbench can become fiddly and intimidating versus a simple page router. MITIGATION: ship 3 one-key presets (Triage/Debug/Catalog) as the default muscle-memory; free docking is power-user opt-in via ⌘\; persist layout so users rarely re-arrange. The danger is users never discovering panes are dockable — surface lens chips prominently in the Run pane header so the common path (swap-in-place) needs zero dock knowledge.

CROSS-FILTER FETCH STORM: every `opIdx` change calls `getReplay(...cursor=idx...)`. Rapid scrubbing could hammer the endpoint. MITIGATION: the endpoint returns the FULL `actions[]` on first load, so fold `stateAt(idx)` CLIENT-SIDE (port `_fold_replay_state`) for scrubbing and only re-request on run change — the server fold is the source of truth but the client re-fold is provably identical (pure). Debounce play-mode.

TOUCHED-BY SCOPE OVERCLAIM: the join is client-side over loaded runs only (`get_vfs_ops` filters by session+run; no `/api/touched-by`, no path filter). 'Touched by N runs' could imply a metastore-wide index. MITIGATION: every touched-by header reads 'in this workspace's loaded runs'; cross-run requires fetching each run's actions and unioning — show a 'load more runs to widen' affordance, never imply all-history.

HONESTY TIERS MUST SURVIVE DENSITY: a dense dark workbench tempts dropping the solid/muted/dimmed distinction to save pixels. MITIGATION: bake the tiers into shared primitives (border style + text opacity + chip), not per-screen styling — is_cache, self-reported intent, client column profiles, pre-stamp op→step always muted; hosted intent / provenance graph / live SQL / latency phases always a dimmed 'not yet' ghost; never fake fingerprint/revision on disk mounts (omit, don't zero-fill).

INTENT≠EFFECT FALSE POSITIVES: a naive heuristic flagging mismatches will erode trust if it cries wolf. MITIGATION: fire conservatively (only on explicit live/latest/current-vs-cache or named-path-vs-read-path contradictions), never when intent is absent, label every fire 'possible mismatch · heuristic', and tone it as a prompt-to-look not a verdict — designed to upgrade to solid when a cognition plane lands.

LIVE-STREAM LOSSINESS: the live useAgentStream reducer drops tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision, so a workbench bound to the live tail would mis-correlate. MITIGATION: build the Run/Inspector/Lineage panes off the persisted `/replay` + `getSessionTrace` path (authoritative); treat the live stream strictly as a tail-only preview with a 'live — correlation finalizes on persist' note, never as the correlation source.

NO-LIVE-SQL METAPHOR LEAK: a Snowsight-grade Data pane invites users to expect a worksheet they can type SQL into. MITIGATION: the query bar is present-but-disabled with an explicit NotImplementedError tooltip, and the column profiles/Stats are labeled 'derived from files / computed client-side' — the table skin must never imply an engine is answering queries.

name: Mirage Console — Paradigm C: "The Trace Debugger"
thesis: Mirage Console is a Redux-DevTools-for-agent-data-access: a run is not a report you read, it is a recording you scrub. Home is the workspace's run history (Snowsight query-history style); opening a run drops you into a full-screen debugger whose spine is the INTENT+COMMAND timeline (Step→ToolCall→VfsOp), whose floor is a draggable time-travel transport over the persisted `/replay` action stream, and whose right wall is a docked inspector. PROFILE, TIME-TRAVEL, and LINEAGE are not pages — they are three lenses bound to ONE shared cursor (`?run=…&cursor=idx&lens=…`), so the operator-tree cost view, the stateAt(idx) fold/diff, and the touched-by join all describe the same selected VfsOp. The whole thing answers one question — "model mistake or data mistake?" — by making intent (self-reported, muted) and effect (the observed byte, solid) sit on the same card with an INTENT≠EFFECT flag, and by letting any VfsOp cross-link straight into the Snowflake-style Data View (catalog → table-detail → column profile) and back via the reverse touched-by list. Everything is built on what the server actually returns today; honesty tiers (solid / muted / dimmed) are a literal visual language, never decoration.
composition:
ONE single-page app, dark/dense/keyboard-first, composed as a persistent SHELL wrapping a route-driven center. The shell never unmounts; only the center swaps, so the cursor/selection survives navigation.

SHELL (always-on, three fixed bands):
• TOP CONTEXT BAR (44px, the Snowflake role+warehouse / Databricks compute+catalog analog): [Mirage ◆] · Workspace dropdown (e.g. `northhill_corp`) · branch chip `● TEST` (quiet, amber=LIVE; promote is Cmd-K-only, never a button) · ——— center: breadcrumb of where you are (`Runs / run_a1f… / TIME-TRAVEL @ idx 14`) · ——— right: nav switch [Home] [Data] · global ⌘K · session/restore dot. The bar scopes EVERY surface — Home, Run, Data, Compare all read within this workspace+branch; switching workspace re-roots all of them (workspace→session persistence is server-side and survives switches — stronger than browser-storage Recents; we say so in a tooltip).
• LEFT RAIL (collapsible, 52px icon / 200px labeled): Home(run history) · Data(catalog) · Compare · Investigation · — · Recents (last 5 runs as chips). The Lineage lens is deliberately NOT a nav item — it is the cross-link that makes Data⇄Runs bidirectional (Databricks puts lineage on the table AND an up/downstream link on the job).
• CENTER (routed): Home | Run debugger | Data view | Compare | Investigation.
• BOTTOM: only the Run debugger paints the TRANSPORT BAR (36px) here; other routes leave it empty.

ROUTES (permalinkable): `/` Home · `/runs/:sessionId?run=&cursor=&lens=&sel=` Run debugger (lens ∈ profile|timetravel|lineage) · `/data?mount=&path=&col=` Data view · `/compare?a=&b=` · `/investigation/:id`. Cmd-K is a global overlay over any route.

VISUAL SYSTEM (reuse the existing token set verbatim): surface-0/1/2/3 dark greys, text-primary/secondary/muted/faint, mono for all paths/ids/bytes, the 8 mountColor accents (tickets/slack/github/pagerduty/finance/datadog/compliance/customers + neutral fallback), EffectClassTag (scratch/durable-internal/system-of-record/external-effect) and CaptureBadge as-is. THREE HONESTY TIERS render as one consistent treatment everywhere: SOLID = full-opacity text + crisp border (VfsOp leaf, exact diff, mount_prefix+path join, stateAt fold); MUTED = a small ⓘ chip + dotted underline, ~70% opacity (op→step pre-stamp, timestamp merge, derived is_cache, self-reported intent, client-computed column profiles); DIMMED = ~40% opacity + hatched/"not yet" ribbon, non-interactive or preview-only (hosted intent, lineage graph, live SQL, latency-phase split, policy/PII).
navigation:
The mental model is a debugger, so movement is "open a recording, scrub it, pivot the lens, cross to the data, come back" — never a tab-shuffle.

RUN-HISTORY → RUN: Home is a columnar run list (Snowsight query history). Click a row → `/runs/:sessionId?run=…&cursor=last&lens=timetravel`. The debugger opens at the LAST action (server defaults cursor to total-1) so you land on "the final state" and scrub backward, exactly like opening a Redux session at the latest dispatch.

WITHIN A RUN — three motions:
1. DOWN THE SPINE (causality): click any Step / ToolCall / VfsOp row in the left timeline → sets the cursor to that op's idx, re-folds state, rings the row. ↑/↓ steps actions; ⇧↑/⇧↓ jumps step boundaries.
2. ALONG TIME (the transport): drag the bottom playhead, or ⏮◀▶⏭, or Space=play (animates cursor over real `actions[].timestamp` wall-clock at 1×/2×/4×). The cursor is THE single source of truth — timeline, inspector, profile-tree highlight, and lineage panel all re-derive from it. `[` `]` step the cursor; `Home`/`End` jump to first/last.
3. ACROSS LENSES (depth, same cursor): a lens segmented-control [PROFILE · TIME-TRAVEL · LINEAGE] swaps what the CENTER+INSPECTOR show for the SAME selected VfsOp. Switching lens never moves the cursor. `1`/`2`/`3` hotkeys.

RUN ⇄ DATA (the bridge, both directions):
• VfsOp → Data: every VfsOp leaf and the inspector carry [↗ Data]. Click → `/data?mount=…&path=…`, scrolled to that path's table/file detail with its touched-by panel lit. Your run is remembered (a "← back to run_a1f @ idx 14" pill pins top-left of Data).
• Data → Run: in the Data view's "Touched by N runs" panel, each op row deep-links back to `/runs/:sessionId?run=…&cursor=<that idx>&lens=timetravel`, jumping the cursor onto that op and ringing it.

RUN → COMPARE: "Compare" on a run (or Cmd-K) opens `/compare?a=runA&b=runB` — two debugger spines side by side sharing a synced cursor-by-step.

RUN → INVESTIGATION: ⌘⇧S "Pin to investigation" from any selected op/diff/flag adds a card (op + cursor permalink + your note) to the saved-findings notebook.

intentCommand:
THE INTENT+COMMAND CARD (directive 1) — the primary run-inspection unit. Grain = Step(intent) → [ToolCall(command) → VfsOps]: one intent row per step, command+effect repeating per tool call (one step can emit several commands, so it is collapsible, NOT a rigid 1:1). Used in the left By-Step timeline, the Time-Travel DIFF tab, the Profile node detail, and the right inspector — one component, four homes.

DATA SOURCING (all real, via the stamped chain): INTENT = steps.reasoning (folded from AG-UI THINKING). COMMAND = tool_calls.args + tool_name (the exec string). EFFECT = the VfsOp leaf from /replay (op·path·source·bytes·is_cache·fingerprint·revision) + tool_calls.exit_code. Joined by the stamped tool_call_id. Verbatim reasoning + full stdout come from getSessionTrace, revealed on demand.

COLLAPSED CARD (default):
  ┌─ Step 3 · ● step-name · 1.2s · 2 cmds ───────────────────────────┐
  │ INTENT  ⓘ self-reported · AG-UI THINKING                          │  ← MUTED chip; reasoning 2-line clamp
  │   "read the live checkout dashboard to correlate the deploy"      │
  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ ▾ COMMAND  $ cat /s3/dashboards/checkout.json     exit 0 · 6ms     │  ← solid
  │     └ EFFECT  read · /s3/dashboards/checkout_2023.json             │  ← the VfsOp leaf, solid; click → cursor jumps to its idx
  │              s3 · 4.2 KB · rev R3 · etag-9a1f · [cache] ⓘ          │
  │     ⚑ INTENT≠EFFECT — "live" intent vs cached read of a 2023 path  │  ← amber flag (see below)
  │ ▸ COMMAND  $ jq '.errors' …                       exit 0 · 2ms     │  ← 2nd command collapsed (proves Step→[cmds] grain)
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE (one click each, never crowds the default):
  • "▸ verbatim" under INTENT → expands the full reasoning text (getSessionTrace THINKING).
  • "▸ full stdout" on a COMMAND → expands tool_calls.result (reuse ToolCallRow's pre block).
  • clicking an EFFECT row → time-travels the cursor to that VfsOp's idx and opens its DIFF.

THE INTENT≠EFFECT FLAG (powers "model mistake vs data mistake?"): a CONSERVATIVE client heuristic comparing self-reported intent text vs the observed op — fires on e.g. reasoning says "live"/"latest"/"current" but effect is is_cache=true; or reasoning names path A but the VfsOp read path B; or "production" vs a path containing "2023"/"staging". Rendered as a SOLID amber inline flag (the effect is observed truth) with a muted explainer. NEVER fires when intent is absent (no claim → no contradiction). Tooltip: "Heuristic — possible mismatch, not a verdict." This is the single highest-value pixel in the product: model error = intent wrong but data fine; data error = intent right but the bytes/source/freshness wrong.

INTENT≠EFFECT vs HONEST DEGRADATION: 
  • When steps.reasoning is EMPTY: the INTENT row shows "No stated intent for this step" (muted italic) — never fabricated, never LLM-summarized.
  • The "self-reported · AG-UI THINKING" chip is the muted tier and reserves the SOLID "observed intent" slot for a future cognition plane — when a hosted model gateway emits observed cognition, the SAME row flips to a solid chip with NO layout change. EFFECT and COMMAND are always solid (observed I/O). This is the clean-upgrade contract: today's honesty boundary is visible, tomorrow's ground truth drops in without a redesign.

SKIP-ACTION WHAT-IF: toggle 'skip' on a read action; the fold re-computes client-side under a 'Hypothetical: action 9 skipped' banner with one-click revert — answers 'did that later write actually depend on this read?' without re-running anything (honest: a pure state re-fold, NOT a re-drive; disabled for backing-FS-dependent ops).

EXPORT/IMPORT A RECORDING: ⤓ exports a .mirage-session.json (actions[] + getSessionTrace events + mount manifest); a teammate imports it and scrubs the exact same cursor offline — the bug repro becomes a portable, deterministic artifact (labeled 'scrub limited to overlay/reads/run; backing pinned at stand-up').
CMD-K AS THE SPINE OF NAVIGATION: jump path↔run↔cursor↔lens by typing; it is also the ONLY place to promote TEST→LIVE (governance demoted to a quiet, deliberate keystroke, never a tempting button).
risks: Lens-as-pivot-on-one-cursor is powerful but cognitively dense; a first-time user may not grasp that switching PROFILE/TIME-TRAVEL/LINEAGE keeps the same selected op. Mitigation: a persistent 'selected op' anchor chip in the inspector header that never changes across lenses + a one-time coach-mark.

The INTENT≠EFFECT heuristic is the headline feature but is a fragile string heuristic (no semantic NLP). False positives erode trust faster than false negatives. Mitigation: conservative triggers only, always-muted 'possible mismatch — not a verdict' label, never fire on absent intent, and let the user dismiss/flag-as-wrong (feeding nothing today, but honest).

'Touched by N runs' silently means 'N runs loaded in THIS workspace' (client-side union of actions[], no server lineage index). Users may read it as all-history provenance. Mitigation: explicit footer on every lineage panel + a count-tooltip; never draw transitive table→table edges; the [graph ⤢] is dimmed/preview only.

Client-side column profiling over data.jsonl can be heavy for events (5,000 rows / 762KB) and misleading if it silently samples. Mitigation: cap+sample with a visible 'computed from N sampled rows' header, all profile widgets muted, and the table-level stats.json (row_count/size) shown solid alongside so the authoritative numbers are never confused with derived ones.

The transport/time-travel metaphor invites an expectation of re-execution (re-run, edit-and-replay). mirage only re-folds persisted state. Mitigation: 'Hypothetical … re-folded' banners, a disabled-with-tooltip skip on backing-dependent ops, and import labeled 'scrub limited to overlay/reads/run'. Never imply a live re-drive.

Reusing the live useAgentStream path anywhere in the debugger would silently drop tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision and corrupt the correlation chain and diff. Mitigation: the debugger is wired exclusively to /replay + getSessionTrace; the live stream is treated as a tail-only preview on the (de-emphasized) New-Run flow, flagged where shown.

The disabled query bar in the Data view risks looking broken or like an unfinished feature. Mitigation: style it as an intentional 'designed, not yet wired' affordance with the explicit NotImplementedError tooltip and the 'derived from files / no live SQL' note adjacent — turning a limitation into an honesty signal.

Four regions + four-deep card disclosure + bottom transport is a lot of chrome at small widths. Mitigation: inspector and left rail are collapsible, the transport is the last to hide, and Cmd-K provides a keyboard escape hatch so power users can drive without the panels.
